newsitem.title: USA: Texas electricity prices rise with outages, natgas.
newsitem.headline: Texas electricity prices rise with outages, natgas.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were higher Monday with constraints from plant outages and higher natural gas prices, industry sources said.

Natural gas prices were reported to have risen by 10 cents or more due to production shut-ins in preparation for Tropical Storm Joesephine, which was moving towards the northeastern coast of the Gulf of Mexico.
ERCOT electricity prices were also pushed higher by plant outages, the brokers and marketers said.

Lower Colorado River Authority's 430 megawatt (MW) Ferguson gas plant was expected to return to service on Tuesday. Texas Utilities' 1,150 MW Comanche Peak nuclear unit 1 was also shut over the weekend for an expected 42 days for refueling and maintenance.
On-peak firm ERCOT power for Tuesday delivery was talked at $20.00-22.50 from next-day discussion last week at $17.80-18.80, the brokers and marketers said.
Off-peak firm next-day power was said to be talked in the $10.00-14.00 range from $10.00-11.00 last week, the sources said.
November ERCOT power was talked higher at $19.50-20.00 from $18.00-19.00 last week, the sources said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
